### **Job Description and Duties**


The Research Data Specialist II (RDS II) independently performs technical research and statistical work necessary to accomplish the objectives and tasks of the Department of Developmental Services (Department). The RDS II collects, validates, compiles, analyzes and interprets data provided by other departmental units and regional centers (RCs). The RDS II is responsible for complex technical research functions related to department programs, including Employment Services, and conducts point\-in\-time, trend and multivariate analysis of consumer data on a wide range of topics related to services provided through the State’s network of developmental services. The RDS II must have a strong understanding of research and statistical methods.  

  

  

***Effective July 1, 2025, State employees are subject to a salary reduction of three percent in exchange for five hours per month of the Personal Leave.***
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Under Government Code 14200, this position is a hybrid, in\-office/telework position, and may be subject to change. Incumbent can be required to report to the office, or any designated location at any time. Telework agreements can be modified and/or cancelled at any time.
  

  

Pursuant to California Government Code requirements, candidates must be residents of the State of California at the time of appointment.
  

  

All commute expenses to the reporting location will be the responsibility of the selected candidate.  

This position requires lawful authorization to work in the United States. The Department does not sponsor employment visas for this position.
  

  

This position requires the incumbent to maintain consistent and regular attendance, communicate effectively while working with the public, community members, management, staff, and control agencies; develop and maintain knowledge and skills related to specific tasks, methodologies, materials, tools and equipment; complete assignments in a timely and efficient manner; and adhere to departmental policies and procedures.

jobs.title: Civic Data Analyst (Sustainable Mobility)
jobs.description:
### **Description**

  

Alta Planning \+ Design seeks a **Civic Data Analyst (Sustainable Mobility)** for our **Los Angeles** office. This position is a great opportunity for someone who believes in the importance of active, multimodal, and sustainable transportation and who is interested in growing their career as a professional working at the intersection of civic data and sustainability. If you are looking to join an innovative organization and do work that connects people to places while advancing social justice, safety, and environmental resilience, apply with Alta today!  

  

**About Alta**  

  

Alta is a mission\-driven company working to mitigate climate change and advance safety and social justice by shaping sustainable, people\-centered communities. We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.
  

Founded in 1996, Alta was at the forefront of the active transportation movement and has spent nearly 30 years partnering with communities to imagine a more connected, resilient, and inclusive future. Today, with more than 225 staff across the United States and beyond, we are a global leader in creating environments that support everyday life, strengthen human connection, and respond to the challenges of a changing world. Alta offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines, contribute to meaningful work at every scale, and be part of a team committed to making lasting, positive change for people and the places they call home.### **Day to Day**

  

Serve as a technical expert and analyst across various disciplines, project types, and regions. Develop prototypes of repeatable analysis in R, Python, and GIS to advance place\-based sustainable transportation solutions. Over time, foster an entrepreneurial approach to analysis through staff training, research, tool development, and custom web applications.  

Engage across Alta’s disciplines to understand data analytics needs, priorities, and expectations, fostering a data\-informed decision\-making culture. Lead the development of new analytical products that align with the firm's objectives and the multidisciplinary nature of the practice. Collaborate closely with planners, designers, and engineers in tasks related to data analysis and visualization, ensuring the developed solutions bring valuable mobility insights and can scale organization wide.  

Delve into data analysis and visualization components of client projects and R\&D efforts, employing complex methodologies. Address mobility and access challenges through innovative analytical solutions, and articulate data\-driven narratives effectively through reports, technical memos, and presentations. Be proactive in identifying labor\-intensive processes and analysis, exploring avenues to streamline and automate them to create organization\-wide value Work on a range of projects including active transportation plans, safety action plans, complete streets planning, safe routes to school, new mobility plans, and economic benefit studies. Each day, you will keep a community\-focused perspective by pushing forward solutions that help communities inform narratives about people, address multifaceted community goals, prepare communities for change, and build a more just transportation system.### **Qualifications**

  

**Required**  

  

This position requires a combination of skills, experience and education including, but not limited to* Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science or another quantitative field with demonstrated experience in the transportation planning field, OR a Bachelor’s Degree in Planning, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, or Engineering with some experience in the software development and/or data science fields.
* **Proficiency in Python and/or R, SQL**
* **Proficiency in Quantitative Analysis:** A solid background in data analysis, cross tabulation, and data interpretation is essential. Candidates should be able to apply data driven techniques to inform evidence\-based decision\-making in planning and design contexts.
* Strong understanding of databases, GIS, coding, and familiarity with transportation planning at an advanced level.
* GIS Proficiency \- both open\-source (PostGIS, QGIS, geopandas, etc.) and the ESRI suite (ArcGISPro, Spatial Analyst, Network Analyst, etc.).
* Ability to create informative data visualizations through code (e.g. D3, ggplot, matplotlib, plotly, kepler.gl, etc.).
* Experience designing, implementing, and documenting analytical solutions using code. Ability to execute an analysis entirely with code.
* Data specifications \& database acronyms like OSM, MDS, GTFS, GBFS, GPS, CDS don’t scare you.
* Proficient in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, similar products.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.

There are a number of additional skills, experience, and education that would be beneficial to this position including, but not limited to:* Master’s Degree in Urban Planning, Statistics, Data Science, Engineering, Math, or Social Sciences
* 1\+ years of experience in a consulting environment or public entity. You have experience working on responses to public sector requests for proposals.
* AICP Certification.
* Experience using Deltek VantagePoint.
* Active participation in industry\-relevant professional associations and committees.
* Demonstrated work of applied statistics or machine learning techniques to transportation challenges.
* Basic familiarity with deploying analytical solutions over the web with the use of Flask, Django, Fast\-API, Tableau, PowerBI, ArcGIS Enterprise, or R\-Shiny.

  

### **What We Offer**

 **Flexible Schedule**
Alta offers a flexible, hybrid work

jobs.description:
Job Posting: Senior Environmental Scientist



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-524940* 

Senior Environmental Scientist
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)
$7,820\.00 \- $10,732\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **7/27/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you want to conserve California’s natural resources in the work you perform every day? You can have an impact by working collaboratively to help fulfill the Department of Fish and Wildlife's mission.
  

Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) employees are committed to managing and protecting California’s diverse wildlife and the habitats upon which they depend. California is one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. As such, The Department of Fish and Wildlife values diverse employees working together to protect nature for all Californians. CDFW is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where all backgrounds, cultures and personal experiences can thrive and connect others to our critical mission.
  

CDFW's Northern Region Cannabis Enforcement Program (CEP) is looking for a highly motivated Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to work with a dedicated team of natural resource professionals to conserve sensitive habitat by regulating both illicit and legal cannabis farms in Humboldt, Mendocino, Trinity, and Del Norte counties.  

  

  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will work in close cooperation with CDFW's Law Enforcement Division (LED), the Regional Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB), county code enforcement offices, State Waterboard Division of Water Rights, the Department of Cannabis Control, and local law enforcement offices. The incumbent's primary responsibility will be to lead environmental assessments (i.e. document impacts to natural resources) during specialized cannabis cultivation site investigations. However, the work does not simply end with the environmental assessment. This position will often maintain a leadership role in seeing cannabis cultivation sites through to complete site remediation and/or joining California's legal market. This requires the Senior ES Specialist to conduct environmental compliance and monitoring of sites, including driving and operating a vehicle for official state business, and to work collaboratively with CDFW's Cannabis Grants Program to fund eligible, high priority sites, and effectively communicate courses of action with responsible parties and the public.  

  

  

There will never be a dull day on the job as you see new lands, meet interesting people, and work with great scientists all focused on conserving California's public trust resources!  

  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

  

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.  

  

  

Link to Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) Exam: CalCareers  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Ability to work unusual and/or long hours; work consecutive days in the office at a computer; use Microsoft Office Suite and have familiarity with Esri software; travel frequently; spend multiple/consecutive days in the field assessing habitat conditions in adverse weather or terrain, with occasional overnight camping; walking in and through rural terrain where outdoor cannabis cultivation occurs; hiking over rough terrain with no vehicle access; operating a 4WD vehicle off highway, over rough terrain on a weekly basis; operate an all\-terrain vehicle occasionally. As a condition of employment, the incumbent shall possess a valid driver’s license to operate a State vehicle, wear an appropriate uniform consistent with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) for various work situations, such as field surveys and work with public interaction, within and outside the Region as required by the supervisor.  

  

  

Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.

jobs.description:
At MacKay, we believe great people are the foundation of our growth and success.



We are in an exciting phase of expansion, creating new opportunities for our employees to take on meaningful work, collaborate across disciplines, and build long\-term careers. Whether your role is technical or part of our support services team, you play an important role in delivering high\-quality work and helping our projects succeed.


Engineering Analytics, now part of MacKay, is seeking a motivated and relationship\-focused full\-time **Associate or Project Hydrogeologist** to join our team in San Diego, CA. This role will have a mix of office and field\-based responsibilities across a broad range of multi\-year projects for our industrial, aerospace, and governmental clients.



This role is being posted at multiple levels, from Associate Hydrogeologist to Project Hydrogeologist. Level and pay are commensurate with experience.



Join a firm where people stay and where new teammates are genuinely invested. You'll work on technically challenging environmental projects for nationally recognized aerospace, defense, and industrial clients while enjoying the flexibility of a hybrid schedule, close collaboration with experienced colleagues, and the opportunity to take on increasing responsibility as you advance in your career. We've built a team with exceptional continuity, deep technical expertise, and a genuine commitment to one another's success. If you're looking for a place where you can truly grow, we'd love to hear from you.



Key Responsibilities vary by level, with a Project Hydrogeologist providing some oversight and delegation of responsibilities:


* Prepare conceptual models and support fate and transport modeling activities
* Participate in and lead field programs, including well installation, aquifer testing, soil gas sampling, indoor air sampling, and pilot testing
* Evaluate remedial alternatives
* Tabulate, evaluate, and interpret air, soil vapor, soil, surface water, sediment, and groundwater data
* Assess remedial action performance data
* Oversee compliance monitoring field programs and prepare compliance monitoring reports
* Prepare cost estimates and specifications
* Direct and coordinate with analytical laboratories for the analysis of environmental media samples
* Participate in large multi\-disciplinary team projects
* Utilize various software used in the evaluation, design, and preparation of deliverables
* Apply scientific standards, codes, regulations, and company procedures to assigned work
* Assist with project documentation, permitting, and coordination activities
* Coordinate with internal project teams, agencies, consultants, and clients as appropriate
* Support quality assurance and quality control processes
* Communicate professionally with coworkers, clients, agencies, and project stakeholders
* Participate in continuous improvement efforts related to scientific principles and engineering standards, workflows, and technical procedures


Minimum Qualifications for Associate Hydrogeologist:


* Bachelor of Science in geology, hydrogeology, engineering geology, or related environmental science
* Geologist\-In\-Training (GIT) certification
* 2 to 5 years of experience, with a minimum of 1 year of field experience
* Proficient in Excel
* Experience with GIS and associated data management
* Ability to learn and adapt
* Ability to work on multiple project tasks concurrently
* Solid organizational, verbal, and written communication skills
* Ability to establish and maintain relationships with multi\-disciplinary team members


Additional Qualifications for Project Hydrogeologist:


* California Professional Geologist or the ability to obtain reciprocity within a reasonable time frame
* 5\+ years of experience, including management experience


Preferred Qualifications:


* 40\-hour HAZWOPER certification
* Advanced Excel experience using Macros and Power Query
* First aid/CPR trained
* Understanding of groundwater modeling software
* California Certified Hydrogeologist (applies to Project Hydrogeologist)

### **Why Join MacKay?**



A people\-first culture  

At MacKay, we put people first. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can grow, contribute, and do their best work. We support well\-being, encourage balance, and create space for people to succeed both professionally and personally.



Meaningful work and real impact  

Our teams take on complex infrastructure and environmental challenges that support critical systems and shape the places where people live and work. Every role contributes to delivering that work and making it successful.



Growth and opportunity  

We are in an exciting phase of growth, expanding across geographies, services, and markets. That growth creates opportunities for our employees to take on new challenges, build their careers, and contribute in new ways as the company evolves.



A strong and trusted foundation  

Built on more than 50 years of experience, MacKay has developed a reputation for quality work, strong relationships, and dependable results. You'll be part of a team with a solid foundation and a clear direction for the future.



Opportunities to share in success  

We provide opportunities for employees to participate in ownership and build long\-term financial value as the company grows.


### **Our Values**



At MacKay, our values guide how we work, collaborate, and support one another.


* Honesty. We build trust through transparency, integrity, and accountability.
* Dedication. We are committed to the success of our team members, clients, and communities.
* Relationships. We foster lasting connections that strengthen our work and the teams around us.

### **Who We Are**



MacKay is an infrastructure and environmental services firm built on more than 50 years of experience and a growing collective of expertise.



We are in an exciting phase of growth, expanding our reach, strengthening our capabilities

Dyna Builders is a Seattle\-based designer and builder of high\-quality, custom homes. Our projects traverse aesthetic boundaries and are not limited to a particular style; instead, we respect a home's character and strive to make it the best it can be. We specialize in high\-end residential and floating home design and construction.

**Summary Description:**

Under the overall direction of the PM, the PC coordinates work and communication with architects, designers, on\-site Superintendent(s), subcontractors, vendors, and directly with the clients, to ensure each project in the portfolio runs smoothly, professionally, on\-time, and within the established budget. We have an open office environment, and the PC is required to visit the Dyna project sites throughout the Seattle area and interact directly with Dyna clients and other members of the Dyna team, as needed.

**Essential Functions, Duties \& Responsibilities:**

· Works with Dyna’s team of PMs to coordinate the day\-to\-day logistics of each project including direct interactions with Dyna clients, sometimes in their homes, sometimes at the Dyna office.

· Provides semi\-monthly labor summaries and submit to PM within a day to ensure efficient and timely client billings.

· Prepares and executes meeting notes and coordinates with responsible parties for follow\-up items. Ensures meeting minute recaps are sent to the PMs within two days, and then issued to the project’s team (Client, architect, interior designer) within three days.

· Coordinate “Construction Online” tasks and organization; creating project folders, uploading final finish schedules and documents, including weekly meeting notes. Also includes tracking of daily superintendent reports, weekly project pictures and safety documentation. Inform PM of deficiencies.

· Coordinate w/ PM and Accounts Payable in setting up new vendor \& subcontractor agreements before subcontractor performs any work. The PC may follow these steps if they are initiating a vendor/subcontractor agreement.

Manages material delivery schedules; identify any issues that don’t conform to plan specifications or damage and report these issues to the PM. · Provide Client Homeowner Manual at project’s Substantial Completion timeframe, or once Client moves into home.

· Creates new Invoice and Labor Summary excel documents at project start up, for billings.

· Creates any finish and fixture schedules not provided by the designer, for procurement and tracking purposes.

· Manages job mobilization start up tasks, including porta potty scheduling, water jug delivery, no parking street signs, on\-site job safety signs, neighborhood letters, client contact set up, Construction Online project set up, and creating PM/Super Binders.

· Sends documents and contracts on DocuSign at all phases of project; Pre\-Construction Subcontracts, Master Contract, Change Orders, Substantial Completion documents, etc. Saves signed contracts to server and helps manage deliverables with PM.

· Coordinate with Interior Designer or Architect if VE (value engineering) alternatives are needed to stay within budget.

· Order samples of finishes/hardware/materials if requested by Client or PM.

· Confirm with Interior Designer that specified fixtures/hardware include all parts \& pieces required for installation (i.e., Rough in parts, electrical drivers, accessory parts).

· Coordinates the selection and procurement of non\-decorative fixtures in a project. This includes but is not limited to architectural lighting (can lights, LED lighting, puck lights, wall lights), outlets, and certain door/cabinet hardware.

· Helps PM schedule subcontractors on site. For example, scheduling install of slabs, tile, wallpaper, closet systems, shower glass, mirrors, appliances. Includes managing subcontractors’ scope of work based on specifications \& design requirements.

· Work alongside Service Department on past project’s warranty work. Serve as active PC/PM on Service Department smaller projects.

· Coordinate project permitting for street use, Right of Way, parking signs, and restricted access with the City of Seattle (SDIC). PC is expected to maintain their own account on the SDCI website for permitting needs.

Job Posting: Senior Environmental Scientist



Department of Fish and Wildlife


JC\-524940* 

Senior Environmental Scientist
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)
$7,820\.00 \- $10,732\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **7/27/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you want to conserve California’s natural resources in the work you perform every day? You can have an impact by working collaboratively to help fulfill the Department of Fish and Wildlife's mission.
  

Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) employees are committed to managing and protecting California’s diverse wildlife and the habitats upon which they depend. California is one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. As such, The Department of Fish and Wildlife values diverse employees working together to protect nature for all Californians. CDFW is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where all backgrounds, cultures and personal experiences can thrive and connect others to our critical mission.
  

CDFW's Northern Region Cannabis Enforcement Program (CEP) is looking for a highly motivated Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to work with a dedicated team of natural resource professionals to conserve sensitive habitat by regulating both illicit and legal cannabis farms in Humboldt, Mendocino, Trinity, and Del Norte counties.  

  

  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will work in close cooperation with CDFW's Law Enforcement Division (LED), the Regional Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB), county code enforcement offices, State Waterboard Division of Water Rights, the Department of Cannabis Control, and local law enforcement offices. The incumbent's primary responsibility will be to lead environmental assessments (i.e. document impacts to natural resources) during specialized cannabis cultivation site investigations. However, the work does not simply end with the environmental assessment. This position will often maintain a leadership role in seeing cannabis cultivation sites through to complete site remediation and/or joining California's legal market. This requires the Senior ES Specialist to conduct environmental compliance and monitoring of sites, including driving and operating a vehicle for official state business, and to work collaboratively with CDFW's Cannabis Grants Program to fund eligible, high priority sites, and effectively communicate courses of action with responsible parties and the public.  

  

  

There will never be a dull day on the job as you see new lands, meet interesting people, and work with great scientists all focused on conserving California's public trust resources!  

  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

  

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.  

  

  

Link to Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) Exam: CalCareers  

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Ability to work unusual and/or long hours; work consecutive days in the office at a computer; use Microsoft Office Suite and have familiarity with Esri software; travel frequently; spend multiple/consecutive days in the field assessing habitat conditions in adverse weather or terrain, with occasional overnight camping; walking in and through rural terrain where outdoor cannabis cultivation occurs; hiking over rough terrain with no vehicle access; operating a 4WD vehicle off highway, over rough terrain on a weekly basis; operate an all\-terrain vehicle occasionally. As a condition of employment, the incumbent shall possess a valid driver’s license to operate a State vehicle, wear an appropriate uniform consistent with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901\) for various work situations, such as field surveys and work with public interaction, within and outside the Region as required by the supervisor.  

  

  

Telework is up to the discretion and approval of the supervisor and will be consistent with current telework policies.
